https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/co.summary: Herbalife Korea’s next phase of growth will depend on lasting customer relationships rather than individual transactions, Herbalife Korea General Manager Sean Chung said, as the company marks its 30th anniversary in Korea by overhauling distributor compensation and introducing AI tools. Since entering Korea in 1996, Herbalife has expanded from weight management products into everyday nutrition, protein, sports nutrition and beauty-related wellness as consumer priorities have evolved.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/co.summary_zh: 康宝莱韩国总经理肖恩·钟表示，康宝莱韩国下一阶段的增长将取决于持久的客户关系，而非单笔交易。目前，公司正值进入韩国市场30周年之际，全面调整经销商报酬机制并推出人工智能工具。自1996年进入韩国以来，随着消费者需求的演变，康宝莱已从体重管理产品拓展至日常营养、蛋白质、运动营养及美容健康领域。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/co.body: Herbalife Korea’s next phase of growth will depend on lasting customer relationships rather than individual transactions, Herbalife Korea General Manager Sean Chung said, as the company marks its 30th anniversary in Korea by overhauling distributor compensation and introducing AI tools. The company’s history has been about helping Koreans build healthy nutrition habits, he said, arguing that sustainable growth comes from maintaining trust beyond a single sale. Since entering Korea in 1996, Herbalife has expanded from weight management products into everyday nutrition, protein, sports nutrition and beauty-related wellness as consumer priorities have evolved. Its first decade centered on its flagship Formula 1 shake brand, balancing nutrient intake and healthy eating habits in a market dominated by physical stores and face-to-face sales. From 2006 and 2015, the rapid growth of online shopping and hypermarkets intensified competition. During this period, Herbalife emphasized ongoing communication and communities that helped customers maintain habits they found difficult to sustain on their own, extending its role beyond simply selling products. To support this approach, one-on-one coaching by independent distributors remains central, according to Chung. Maintaining healthy routines requires ongoing effort. Distributors assess customers’ goals, diets and circumstances to help them achieve healthier lifestyles. They explain nutritional needs before recommending products and tailor usage guidance to individuals, including for weight management and muscle health. After products are delivered, distributors continue to provide encouragement and information to help customers maintain balanced diets and exercise routines. “While conventional retail gives consumers convenient access to a wide range of products, Herbalife seeks to offer personalized nutrition guidance and ongoing coaching,” Chung said in an interview with The Korea Times. Consumer trust also rests on product quality. Herbalife’s Seed to Feed system oversees quality at every stage, from ingredient sourcing to finished products. Its global network of more than 200 scientists, physicians and nutrition specialists supports product development and education. Chung said the company’s distributor training program prohibits exaggerated advertising claims that products can treat diseases. The company also discourages unnecessary purchases and maintains refund policies, linking responsible sales practices to the brand trust it has built over three decades. Herbalife Korea has also invested in building ties with local communities. These efforts include Casa Herbalife, launched in 2007 to support Sang Rok Won, a children’s home. Employees and distributors have volunteered throughout the nearly two-decade initiative, which supports nutrition and healthy development for children. The company also began sponsoring sporting events to promote nutrition and physical activity, starting with a Chuseok ssireum (Korean wrestling) championship in 2008. Its sponsorships have since extended to Korean Baseball Organization club Kiwoom Heroes, the Korea Weightlifting Federation and the Daegu Marathon. Since 2016, Herbalife Korea has also developed partnerships with scientific organizations in Korea. It has worked with the Korean Diabetes Society on coach education involving endocrinology professors, diabetes education nurses and clinical exercise specialists. The partnership was followed by an agreement with the Korean Nutrition Society in 2020 and the establishment of an award supporting young nutrition researchers in 2021. In September this year, the diabetes partnership was expanded to include the Health Confidence program for people with prediabetes. Chung described the anniversary as the starting point for a redesign aimed at the next 30 years. “We did not spend our 30th anniversary simply commemorating the past. We preserved the relationships our people have built while redesigning the structure that keeps those relationships working,” he said. Introduced earlier this year, Herbalife’s new market plan revises distributor compensation, moving away from a relatively uniform global system toward more customized arrangements based on conditions in each operating country. In digitally connected Korea, where side jobs and multiple income streams are common, the company aims to accommodate distributors’ different circumstances and goals, expand opportunities for newcomers and support the growth of existing distributors. AI tools are designed to ease workloads, allowing distributors to spend more time understanding customers’ lifestyles and maintaining communication. HL/Skin.ai, an AI-powered skin analysis system launched alongside the HL/Skin skin care lineup, asks users for their age and skin type before conducting a facial scan via smartphone. Within 60 seconds, it provides an overall skin score covering hydration, blemishes, wrinkles, dark circles, texture, tone, firmness and oiliness, along with corresponding product recommendations. The tools, however, will not replace people, Chung said, emphasizing that understanding individual circumstances and encouraging healthy behavior remain human responsibilities. The operational restructuring has also involved expanding the product lineup. Herbalife24, the company's sports nutrition line launched in Korea in 2016, added Liftoff Powder, a fast-dissolving effervescent vitamin product, last year. This was followed by the launch of HL/Skin in March this year. The expanded portfolio targets a range of needs, including protein intake, muscle health, healthy aging and beauty-related wellness. The product expansion reflects a decade transformed by smartphones, social media and the COVID-19 pandemic, which made online research and shopping part of everyday life. As consumer interests broadened beyond weight loss and appearance to encompass nutrition, exercise, sleep, stress management and skin health, Herbalife expanded its product offerings and scientific expertise to address these evolving needs. Korea is serving as an early proving ground for Herbalife’s evolving strategy. It was among the first markets globally to introduce the new compensation plan, reflecting the company's headquarters' recognition of Korea's strategic importance. “Korea is a market that embraces change quickly and is the first to show that those changes work,” he said. Although Korea’s health supplement market is smaller than those of the United States and China, consumers’ knowledge and willingness to try new products raise the bar for the industry, Chung said. Citing the Korea Health Functional Food Association, he said the domestic market was valued at nearly 6 trillion won ($4.5 billion) last year, with 84 percent of consumers making repeat purchases within a year, indicating that health supplements have become part of everyday consumption. Chung said consumers increasingly scrutinize ingredients, dosages, product quality, scientific evidence and corporate credibility rather than relying on assumptions or recommendations from others. HL/Skin, he added, was developed in response to growing interest among beauty-conscious consumers in managing both their health and appearance. To better serve the Korean market, Herbalife has combined global expertise with ingredients and flavors familiar to local consumers. Formula 1 was introduced in flavors tailored to consumer preferences in different markets, while Red Ginseng Gel sold in Korea uses six-year-old red ginseng grown in Korea. “Korea is a market with strong interest in new products and high standards for quality and trust. This environment drives companies to continually improve products and services,” Chung said. As Korea becomes a super-aged society, healthy longevity is gaining importance beyond simply extending lifespans. Chung emphasized the importance of muscle health, balanced nutrition and regular physical activity. The company is also examining nutritional needs following rapid weight loss with obesity medications, with a focus on balanced nutrient intake and muscle maintenance. For Chung, personalization means moving away from one-size-fits-all recommendations toward products and guidance tailored to individuals' ages, lifestyles and health goals. Digital services should make relevant information easier to access, while coaches and communities should help customers turn recommendations into daily routines. This combination, he said, will underpin the company's focus on personalized nutrition and healthy longevity over the coming decades. “Over the past 30 years, Herbalife has evolved from a company centered on weight-management products into a comprehensive nutrition and wellness company. We now aim to grow into a global premium health and wellness platform combining personalized nutrition, digital technology and people-centered coaching,” Chung said
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/co.title_zh: 康宝莱韩国以30年信任开启新篇章
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/co.body_zh: Herbalife韩国总经理Sean Chung表示，公司在韩国迎来30周年之际，通过全面改革经销商薪酬体系并推出人工智能工具，其下一阶段的增长将取决于持久的客户关系，而非单笔交易。他说，公司的发展历程主要围绕帮助韩国人建立健康营养习惯，并指出，可持续增长来自将信任延续到一次销售之后。自1996年进入韩国以来，随着消费者优先需求的演变，Herbalife已从体重管理产品拓展至日常营养、蛋白质、运动营养和美容健康领域。其第一个十年的重点是旗舰产品Formula 1营养奶昔，该品牌帮助消费者平衡营养摄入与健康饮食习惯；当时的市场主要由实体店和面对面销售主导。从2006年至2015年，网上购物和大型超市的迅速增长加剧了竞争。在此期间，Herbalife重视持续沟通和社群建设，帮助客户维持那些单靠自身难以坚持的习惯，从而将公司的角色从单纯销售产品延伸至更多方面。Chung表示，为支持这一做法，由独立经销商提供的一对一指导仍至关重要。保持健康作息需要持续付出努力。经销商会评估客户的目标、饮食和生活状况，帮助他们实现更健康的生活方式。他们会先解释营养需求，再推荐产品，并针对个人情况提供使用指导，包括体重管理和肌肉健康方面。产品送达后，经销商仍会继续提供鼓励和信息，帮助客户保持均衡饮食和运动习惯。Chung在接受《韩国时报》采访时表示：“传统零售为消费者提供便捷渠道，让他们能够接触种类繁多的产品；Herbalife则希望提供个性化营养指导和持续陪伴。”消费者对产品的信任也建立在质量之上。Herbalife的Seed to Feed体系对从原料采购到成品的每个环节实施质量监督。其由200多名科学家、医生和营养专家组成的全球网络为产品开发和健康教育提供支持。Chung表示，公司的经销商培训项目禁止夸大广告宣传，禁止声称产品可以治疗疾病。公司还劝阻消费者进行不必要的购买，并执行退款政策，将负责任的销售做法与品牌在三十年间建立的信任联系起来。Herbalife韩国还投入精力建设与当地社区的联系。这些工作包括于2007年推出的Casa Herbalife，该项目为儿童之家Sang Rok Won提供支持。近二十年来，员工和经销商一直以志愿方式参与这一项目，帮助儿童改善营养状况并促进健康成长。公司还开始赞助体育赛事，以推广营养和身体活动，2008年首先赞助了中秋节摔跤（韩国式摔跤）锦标赛。此后，其赞助范围扩展至韩国棒球委员会的Kiwoom Heroes、韩国举重联合会和大邱马拉松。自2016年以来，Herbalife韩国还与韩国的科学机构建立合作关系。公司与韩国糖尿病学会合作开展教练培训，由内分泌学教授、糖尿病教育护士和临床运动专家参与。随后，公司于2020年与韩国营养学会达成协议，并于2021年设立奖项，支持青年营养研究人员。今年9月，双方的糖尿病合作关系进一步扩大，将面向糖尿病前期人群的Health Confidence项目纳入其中。Chung表示，这次周年纪念是面向下一个30年的重新设计之起点。他说：“我们并不是只回顾过去来纪念30周年。我们在重新设计支撑这些关系持续运转的架构时，也保留了我们的人员与客户之间建立的联系。”Herbalife今年早些时候推出的新市场计划修订了经销商薪酬方案，摆脱相对统一的全球体系，转向根据各运营国家的实际情况制定更定制化的安排。在数字化程度较高的韩国，兼职和多元收入来源十分普遍，因此公司希望适应经销商不同的处境和目标，为新加入者拓宽机会，并支持现有经销商的发展。人工智能工具旨在减轻工作负担，让经销商能够投入更多时间了解客户的生活方式并维持沟通。HL/Skin.ai是随HL/Skin护肤系列一同推出的人工智能皮肤分析系统，它会先询问用户的年龄和肤质，然后通过智能手机进行面部扫描。不到60秒，系统便会提供综合皮肤评分，涵盖水合度、瑕疵、皱纹、黑眼圈、纹理、肤色、紧致度和油分，并给出相应的产品建议。不过，Chung强调，这些工具不会取代人员；了解个人情况并鼓励健康行为仍然是人类的职责。运营重组还包括扩大产品阵容。公司于2016年在韩国推出运动营养产品线Herbalife24，并于去年新增快速溶解的泡腾维生素产品Liftoff Powder。随后，公司于今年3月推出HL/Skin。扩充后的产品组合涵盖多种需求，包括蛋白质摄入、肌肉健康、健康老龄化和美容健康。产品扩展反映出过去十年中智能手机、社交媒体和COVID-19疫情带来的变化，这些变化使网上研究和购物成为日常生活的一部分。随着消费者的兴趣从减重和外观拓展到营养、运动、睡眠、压力管理和皮肤健康，Herbalife扩大了产品种类和科学专业能力，以满足这些不断演变的需求。韩国正成为Herbalife新战略发展的早期试验场。该公司是最早引入新薪酬方案的市场之一，反映出公司总部对韩国战略重要性的认可。Chung说：“韩国是一个能够迅速接纳变化的市场，也是第一个证明这些变化行得通的市场。”他表示，尽管韩国的健康补充剂市场规模小于美国和中国，但消费者的知识水平以及尝试新产品的意愿提高了行业标准。Chung援引韩国健康机能食品协会的数据称，国内市场去年估值接近6万亿韩元（$4.5 billion），84%的消费者在一年内重复购买，表明健康补充剂已成为日常消费的一部分。Chung表示，消费者越来越仔细审视成分、剂量、产品质量、科学证据和企业信誉，而不再依赖主观臆断或他人的推荐。他补充称，HL/Skin的开发是为回应注重美容的消费者在管理健康与外观方面日益增长的需求。为更好地服务韩国市场，Herbalife将全球专业能力与当地消费者熟悉的原料和口味相结合。Formula 1推出了适应不同市场消费者偏好的口味，在韩国销售的红参凝胶则采用在韩国种植的六年生红参。Chung说：“韩国是一个对新产品兴趣浓厚、对质量和信任要求很高的市场。这种环境促使企业持续改进产品和服务。”随着韩国进入超高龄社会，健康长寿的重要性已不再局限于延长寿命。Chung强调，肌肉健康、均衡营养和规律身体活动十分重要。公司还在研究使用肥胖症药物快速减重后的营养需求，重点关注均衡摄入营养物质和维持肌肉。对Chung而言，个性化意味着不再采用适用于所有人的统一建议，而是根据个人的年龄、生活方式和健康目标量身定制产品与指导。数字服务应当让相关信息更易获取，而教练和社群则应帮助客户把建议转化为日常习惯。他说，这种结合将成为公司未来几十年专注个性化营养和健康长寿的基础。Chung说：“过去30年来，Herbalife从一家以体重管理产品为核心的企业，发展成为一家综合性营养与健康公司。如今我们的目标，是成长为融合个性化营养、数字技术和以人为本指导的全球高端健康与养生平台。”

https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026112204.summary: (서울=연합뉴스) 송진원 기자 = 중국의 국가정보기관이 미국의 대중국 반도체 수출 통제를 우회하고 인공지능(AI) 기술의 핵심인 첨단 반도체 확보를 위한 비밀 작전을 최소 2년 전부터 추진해 온 것으로 전해졌다. 미국 뉴욕타임스(NYT)는 전·현직 해외 정보 당국자들을 인용해 중국 국가안전부 천이신 부장(장관)이 이 작전을 주도하며 자신이 직접 보고받는 실무팀을 구성했다고 21일(현지시간) 보도했다. 이 조직의 핵심 임무는 미국과 그 동맹국의 수출 통제로 중국이 확보하기 어려워진 첨단 반도체 입수를 지원하는 것이다.
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026112204.summary_zh: （首尔＝联合通讯社记者宋镇元）据报道，中国国家情报机构至少从两年前开始推进一项秘密行动，旨在规避美国对华半导体出口管制，并获取人工智能（AI）技术的核心——先进半导体。美国《纽约时报》（NYT）21日（当地时间）援引前现任海外情报官员的话报道称，中国国家安全部情报长（部长）田宜新主导了这项行动，并组建了直接向其汇报的工作团队。该组织的核心任务是为获取中国难以通过美国及其盟国出口管制取得的先进半导体提供支持。
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026112204.body: (서울=연합뉴스) 송진원 기자 = 중국의 국가정보기관이 미국의 대중국 반도체 수출 통제를 우회하고 인공지능(AI) 기술의 핵심인 첨단 반도체 확보를 위한 비밀 작전을 최소 2년 전부터 추진해 온 것으로 전해졌다. 미국 뉴욕타임스(NYT)는 전·현직 해외 정보 당국자들을 인용해 중국 국가안전부 천이신 부장(장관)이 이 작전을 주도하며 자신이 직접 보고받는 실무팀을 구성했다고 21일(현지시간) 보도했다. 이 조직의 핵심 임무는 미국과 그 동맹국의 수출 통제로 중국이 확보하기 어려워진 첨단 반도체 입수를 지원하는 것이다. 중국 기업들이 첨단 반도체를 확보해 중국으로 밀반입하도록 돕는 작업도 포함된다. 글로벌 반도체 산업과 공급망에 대한 정보도 수집하는 것으로 알려졌다. 천 부장은 올해 4월 공산당 간행물에 기고한 글에서 국가안전부의 새로운 임무를 공개적으로 강조했다. 그는 "봉쇄에 맞선 투쟁을 심화하고, AI 혁신, 산업 발전 및 응용을 포괄적으로 추진해야 한다"고 밝혔다. 이어 "핵심 기술의 '차보쯔'(卡脖子·목을 조르는 핵심 기술)' 문제를 해결하는 데 주력해야 한다"면서 "요청하거나 구매하거나 애원해서는 얻을 수 없는" 기술을 확보해야 한다고 강조했다. 이는 미국의 기술 수출통제를 단순한 경제·산업적 제약이 아니라 국가안보 차원의 대응 과제로 규정하고, 정보기관을 동원해 돌파구를 마련하겠다는 의지를 드러낸 것으로 풀이된다. 중국 안보 전문 컨설팅 회사 가노 글로벌의 알렉스 조스케는 "천 부장은 당 지도부와 소속 간부들에게 자신의 기관이 미국과의 AI 경쟁을 장기적이고 최우선 과제로 격상시키고 있음을 시사하고 있다"며 "그는 간부들에게 이 투쟁을 수행할 더 많은 방법을 찾으라고 지시하고 있는 것"이라고 평가했다. 천 부장은 2022년 말 국가안전부장에 임명된 이후 미국 등 서방의 첨단 기술 통제를 중국의 발전을 가로막는 '봉쇄'로 규정하며 대응을 강조해 왔다. 그는 지난해 공산당 간행물 기고문에서도 "강대국 간 기술 경쟁은 가장 치열하고 가장 격렬하며, 가장 중대한 접전 단계에 접어들었다"고 진단했다. 시 주석은 올해 1월 공산당 중앙정치국 회의에서 "우선 분야 핵심 기술 확보를 위한 노력을 강화하기 위해 비상한 조처를 해야 한다"며 "미래 산업 발전을 가로막고 있는 '차보쯔' 문제를 가능한 한 신속히 해결해야 한다"고 강조했다. 시 주석은 AI 발전에 필요한 컴퓨팅 성능 분야에서 미국과의 격차를 좁히기 위해 2023년 중앙 정부 차원에서 중앙과학기술위원회도 설립했다. 2022년 말 미국 상무부가 엔비디아의 첨단 칩이 중국에 직접 수출되는 걸 금지하기 시작한 지 얼마 지나지 않은 시점이다. 이 위원회는 중국 언론 보도에 거의 등장하지 않고 예산과 계획도 공개되지 않지만, 시 주석의 기술적 우위 확보 계획의 원동력이 됐다고 미 중앙정보국(CIA) 출신 중국 전문가 크리스토퍼 K. 존슨은 설명한다. 제보는 카카오톡 okjebo <저작권자(c) 연합뉴스, 무단 전재-재배포, AI 학습 및 활용 금지> 2026/11/22 18:28 송고 2026년11월22일 18시28분 송고
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026112204.title_zh: 中国国家安全部为获取先进芯片，两年前便开始秘密行动
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026112204.body_zh: （首尔=韩联社）记者宋真元=据报道，中国国家情报机构至少从两年前开始推行秘密行动，试图绕开美国针对中国的半导体出口管制，并获取人工智能（AI）技术的核心——先进半导体。美国《纽约时报》（NYT）21日（当地时间）援引前现任海外情报官员的话报道称，中国国家安全部部长陈仪新主导了这项行动，并组建了直接向其汇报的工作团队。该组织的核心任务是协助中国获取因美国及其盟国出口管制而难以取得的先进半导体，工作内容还包括帮助中国企业获取先进半导体并走私进入中国。据称，该组织还搜集有关全球半导体产业和供应链的信息。陈部长在今年4月刊载于共产党刊物的文章中，公开强调了国家安全部的新使命。他表示：“必须深化反封锁斗争，全面推进人工智能创新、产业发展和应用。”他还强调：“必须集中力量解决核心技术的‘卡脖子’问题”，确保掌握“靠请求、购买或乞求都无法获得”的技术。这意味着，美国的技术出口管制被界定为涉及国家安全的应对任务，而不只是经济或产业限制；相关机构将动用情报力量寻找突破口。中国国家安全问题咨询公司 Gano Global 的 Alex Joske 表示：“陈部长表明，其机构已将与美国的人工智能竞争提升为长期且最高优先级的任务。”他评价说：“他已指示官员寻找开展这场斗争的更多方式。”陈部长于2022年末获任国家安全部部长以来，一直强调将美国等西方对先进技术的管制视为阻碍中国发展的“封锁”，并着手应对。他在去年发表于共产党刊物的文章中诊断称：“大国之间的技术竞争已经进入最激烈、最激烈交锋、最重大碰撞的阶段。”习近平总书记在今年1月召开的中央政治局会议上强调：“为加强 efforts 以获取优先领域核心技术，必须采取非常措施。”他表示：“必须尽快解决阻碍未来产业发展的‘卡脖子’问题。”习近平还于2023年从中央政府层面设立了中央科技委员会，以缩小中国在人工智能发展所需计算性能方面与美国的差距。那是在美国商务部开始禁止英伟达先进芯片直接出口中国后不久，即2022年末。中国媒体报道几乎鲜有提及该委员会，其预算和计划也未公开，但美国中央情报局（CIA）出身的中国专家 Christopher K. Johnson 解释称，该委员会已成为习近平获取技术优势计划的推动力量。更多报道请登录 KakaoTalk 账号 okjebo <版权所有(c) 韩联社，未经许可禁止转载、再分发，禁止用于人工智能学习及使用>。2026年11月22日18:28发稿

https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/11/2.body: A fire onboard a Russia n cargo ship that was struck by drones in the Baltic Sea continued to burn through the night even as efforts were made to douse the flames, Finland's coast guard said on Sunday. The Finnish military has said the strike on the Sparta II on Saturday was likely carried out by Ukraine and that the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters where it remains at anchor. The 16 crew members were evacuated onto a nearby Russia n ship. Pictures and video released by the coast guard showed several vessels spraying the Sparta II with water cannons during the night in a bid to put out the flames and cool down containers stacked on its deck. Ukraine has sent waves of military drones towards Russia 's northwest coastal Leningrad region this year, including some that strayed into the airspace of nearby Baltic countries, leading to fears that the war was spilling onto NATO territory. The ship, bound for Russia n exclave Kaliningrad, was damaged in international waters west of Russia 's Gogland island, Finland's Defense Forces have said, corroborating an account by Russia n officials. The risk of further attacks in the Gulf of Finland, a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea, cannot be ruled out, Estonian Navy Commander Ivo Vark told public broadcaster ERR on Sunday. Finland's military said last week it had detected a strike on a Russia n warship in the same area during Ukrainian drone attacks. The Sparta II is a 121-meter Russia n-flagged cargo vessel owned by Russia n shipping company Oboronlogistika that left St. Petersburg on Friday, according to LSEG data. The vessel is subject to U.S. sanctions, according to the U.S. Treasury Department. Oboronlogistika provides logistics services for the Russia n Defense Ministry, according to the company's website. https://leadership.ng/investors-sell-off.title: Investors’ Sell-offs Wipe N2.99trn Off Stock Market
https://leadership.ng/investors-sell-off.summary: N2.99 trillion off the Nigerian stock market last week as profit-taking activities following weeks of strong gains triggered a decline in share prices across several counters. The decline in trading volume and value underscored the cautious disposition of investors amid persistent profit-taking and weakening market sentiment.
https://leadership.ng/investors-sell-off.summary_zh: 上周尼日利亚股市市值缩水2.99万亿奈拉，数周大幅上涨后，获利回吐活动引发多个交易板块股价下跌。成交量和成交额下降凸显出投资者在持续获利回吐和市场情绪转弱之际的谨慎态度。
https://leadership.ng/investors-sell-off.body: Investors’ sell-offs wiped N2.99 trillion off the Nigerian stock market last week as profit-taking activities following weeks of strong gains triggered a decline in share prices across several counters. The benchmark Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) All-Share Index (ASI) fell by 1.83 per cent week-on-week to close at 247,660.74 points, while market capitalisation declined by approximately N2.99 trillion to N160.80 trillion. Consequently, the market’s year-to-date (YTD) return moderated to 59.15 per cent, reflecting the impact of sustained selling pressure on equities. Market sentiment remained weak throughout the week, with market breadth closing negative as 43 stocks declined against 39 gainers, indicating that losses outnumbered advances across the trading floor. Livingtrust Mortgage Bank led the gainers’ table with a 28.76 per cent appreciation to close at N3.00 per share. Chellarams followed with a 20.62 per cent gain to close at N11.70, while International Breweries advanced by 20.24 per cent to close at N10.10 per share. On the losers’ table, Meyer led with a 17.43 per cent decline to close at N14.45 per share. R.T. Briscoe followed with a 16.94 per cent loss to close at N7.60, while Lasaco Assurance shed 10 per cent to close at N1.71 per share. Trading activity also weakened during the week, as investors exchanged 2.366 billion shares valued at N106.363 billion in 159,759 deals, compared with 8.029 billion shares worth N185.358 billion traded in 160,836 deals in the preceding week. The decline in trading volume and value underscored the cautious disposition of investors amid persistent profit-taking and weakening market sentiment. Market analysts, however, described the weekly decline as a healthy correction following the market’s sustained rally, rather than an indication of a fundamental downturn. They noted that profit-taking was expected after an extended period of gains, as investors sought to lock in returns and rebalance their portfolios. However, they cautioned that market sentiment remained fragile, with investors closely monitoring macroeconomic indicators, corporate earnings, interest rate movements and foreign exchange developments for fresh direction. On the market outlook, Sterling Asset Management and Trustees Limited (SAMTL) said the recovery of the equities market would depend largely on renewed investor confidence and buying interest. “The market’s recovery will depend on renewed investor confidence and buying interest. However, continued selling may cause further short-term declines, while lower share prices could attract new buyers,” the firm stated. Similarly, Cowry Assets Management Limited projected cautious trading in the coming week, warning that persistent profit-taking and weak investor sentiment could continue to weigh on market performance. https://leadership.ng/investors-sell-off.title_zh: 投资者抛售令股市市值蒸发2.99万亿奈拉
https://leadership.ng/investors-sell-off.body_zh:
投资者集中抛售令尼日利亚股市上周蒸发2.99万亿奈拉。在连续数周强劲上涨后，投资者获利了结，导致多只股票价格下跌。基准的尼日利亚交易所有限公司（NGX）全股指数（ASI）周环比下跌1.83%，收于247,660.74点；市场总市值约减少2.99万亿奈拉，降至160.80万亿奈拉。因此，该市场年初至今（YTD）的收益率回落至59.15%，反映出持续卖压对股票市场的影响。整个周内，市场情绪依然疲弱，43只股票下跌，39只股票上涨，市场广度收负，显示各交易板块的下跌股数量多于上涨股。Livingtrust Mortgage Bank领涨，股价上涨28.76%，收于每股3.00奈拉。Chellarams紧随其后，股价上涨20.62%，收于11.70奈拉；International Breweries上涨20.24%，收于每股10.10奈拉。跌幅榜方面，Meyer领跌，股价下跌17.43%，收于每股14.45奈拉。R.T. Briscoe紧随其后，股价下跌16.94%，收于7.60奈拉；Lasaco Assurance下跌10%，收于每股1.71奈拉。

当周交易活动也有所减弱。投资者共交易23.66亿股，价值1063.63亿奈拉，成交159,759笔；相比之下，前一周成交80.29亿股，价值1853.58亿奈拉，共进行160,836笔交易。成交量和成交额下降凸显出，在持续获利了结和市场情绪转弱的背景下，投资者态度谨慎。

不过，市场分析人士将周度下跌描述为市场持续上涨后的健康回调，而非基本面恶化的迹象。他们指出，在经历一段较长时间上涨后，投资者通过锁定收益和调整投资组合实现获利了结，属于预期之中的现象。但他们也警告称，市场情绪仍然脆弱，投资者正密切观察宏观经济指标、企业盈利、利率走势和外汇市场 developments，以寻找新的市场方向。

展望市场走势，Sterling Asset Management and Trustees Limited（SAMTL）表示，股票市场能否复苏将在很大程度上取决于投资者信心和买入意愿的重振。该公司称：“市场的复苏将取决于投资者信心和买入意愿的重振。然而，持续卖盘可能导致短期内进一步下跌，而较低的股价可能吸引新的买家。”同样，Cowry Assets Management Limited预计未来一周交易将保持谨慎，并警告称，持续的获利了结和疲弱的投资者情绪可能继续对市场表现构成压力。不过，该公司指出，保险和消费品板块相对稳健的表现能够为市场提供一定支撑。我们掌握前沿资讯。获取实时报道、独家爆料和独家视角，直接推送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，随时随地获取全天候更新→

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: The All Progressives Congress (APC) has renewed efforts to reconcile Benue State Governor Hyacinth Alia and the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), George Akume, amid a prolonged leadership crisis that has divided the party in the state. Mr Alia disclosed this in a post on his verified Facebook page on Sunday, saying he had attended a reconciliation meeting in Abuja convened by the North Central Presidential Reconciliation Committee. The committee is chaired by former Katsina State Governor Ibrahim Shema. The meeting, which lasted about two hours, was attended by Mr Akume, former Benue Governor Gabriel Suswam, Senators Barnabas Gemade, Jack Gyado, and Simon Shango, among other stakeholders. Mr Alia thanked Mr Shema and members of the committee for bringing the leaders together, saying reconciliation required a willingness to listen, speak frankly and continue working together despite differences. “I thank Sen. Shema and his committee for bringing us together. Reconciliation takes a willingness to listen, to speak frankly and to keep working together even where differences remain,” he said. The governor said he would continue engaging with party leaders and stakeholders in the interest of a united APC, while prioritising peace, security and development in Benue. He added that the responsibility the people entrusted to political leaders should guide their actions. Mr Alia did not disclose the specific issues discussed at the meeting or whether the participants had reached any agreement to resolve the crisis. The meeting comes amid a prolonged disagreement between factions of the Benue APC loyal to Mr Alia and Mr Akume, centred on control of the party’s structures and influence over its political affairs. The dispute has produced parallel party executives and competing claims over the leadership of the state chapter. On 4 March, the two camps held separate state congresses in Makurdi. Mr Alia’s faction returned Benjamin Omale as state chairman, while the Akume-aligned faction affirmed the Austin Agada-led executive committee for another four-year term. The factions have also disagreed over political mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. PREMIUM TIMES reported on 15 November that the Director-General of the Tinubu-Alia 2027 Campaign Council, Richard Asema, accused Mr Akume, Minister of Water Resources, Joseph Utsev, and other APC figures of working with opposition politicians through the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu-Shettima 2027. The alliance’s Director-General, Akange Audu, rejected the allegation, describing it as political blackmail. He said the group was an independent platform for mobilising support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election and argued that supporting the president should not be made conditional on supporting Mr Alia. PREMIUM TIMES also reported on 16 November that Mr Alia attributed the APC crisis to his refusal to share state funds with some party chieftains whom he accused of wanting to turn Benue into their private estate. The governor, who made the allegation at the Adamawa State Tiv Day celebration in Yola, did not name the party leaders or provide details of the alleged demand. The latest meeting represents another attempt to bridge the divisions among the party’s leading figures. However, Mr Alia’s account did not indicate whether the reconciliation committee had secured any commitment from the rival camps or agreed on a framework for resolving their differences
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title_zh: APC再次出手调解贝努埃州阿库梅与阿利亚的关系
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body_zh: 进步大会党（APC）重新努力调解贝努埃州州长海阿辛特·阿利亚与联邦政府秘书（SGF）乔治·阿库梅之间的分歧。持续已久的领导层危机已使该党在贝努埃州的队伍分裂。阿利亚先生周日在其经认证的Facebook页面上透露了这一消息，称他出席了在阿布贾举行的一次调解会议，会议由中部北部总统调解委员会召集。该委员会由前卡齐纳州州长易卜拉欣·谢马主持。会议持续约两个小时，出席者包括阿库梅先生、前贝努埃州州长加布里埃尔·苏斯瓦姆、参议员巴纳巴斯·格马德、杰克·贾多和西蒙·尚戈，以及其他利益相关方。阿利亚先生感谢谢马先生和委员会成员促成各方会面，表示调解需要愿意倾听、坦诚发言，并在存在分歧的情况下继续合作。他说：“我感谢谢马参议员及其委员会促成各方会面。调解需要愿意倾听、坦诚发言，即使分歧仍然存在，也要继续合作。”州长表示，为实现团结的APC，他将继续与党内领导人和利益相关方沟通，同时把贝努埃州的和平、安全与发展置于优先位置。他补充说，人民赋予政治领导人的责任应当指导他们的行动。阿利亚先生没有透露会议讨论的具体问题，也没有说明与会者是否就解决危机达成任何协议。此次会议召开之际，忠于阿利亚先生和阿库梅先生的贝努埃州APC派系长期存在分歧，争议核心是对该党组织架构的控制权及其政治事务的影响力。这场争端导致两套并行的党内执行机构并存，双方也对州党组织的领导权提出相互竞争的主张。3月4日，两派分别在庫尔迪举行了州代表大会。阿利亚先生一方推举本杰明·奥马莱再次担任州主席，而与阿库梅结盟的一派则确认由奥斯汀·阿加达领导的执行委员会再任4年。各派还就2027年大选前的政治动员存在分歧。《PREMIUM TIMES》11月15日报道称，Tinubu-Alia 2027竞选委员会主任理查德·阿塞马指控水资源部长阿库梅先生、约瑟夫·乌特塞夫及其他APC人士，正通过“Tinubu-Shettima 2027贝努埃战略联盟”与反对派政治人物合作。该联盟主任阿坎格·阿杜驳斥了这一指控，称其属于政治讹诈。他说，该组织是一个独立平台，旨在动员支持总统博拉·蒂努布连任，并认为支持总统不应以支持阿利亚先生为条件。《PREMIUM TIMES》还于11月16日报道称，阿利亚先生将APC危机归因于他拒绝与党内某些首领分享州政府资金，并指控他们企图把贝努埃州变成自己的私人产业。州长在约拉举行的阿达马瓦州蒂夫日庆典上提出这一指控，但没有点名党内领导人，也没有说明所谓要求的具体内容。此次会议是为弥合该党主要人物之间的裂痕而作出的又一次努力。然而，阿利亚先生的说法并未表明调解委员会是否促使对立派系作出任何承诺，或双方是否就解决分歧的框架达成一致……

https://www.thehindu.com/food/features/s.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription In the South, rice and dal stick together even in conversations: arisi-paruppu in Tamil, akki-bele in Kannada, chorum-parippum in Malayalam, and pappu-annam in Telugu. I grew up loving paruppu. For as long as I can remember, breakfast was hot rice with a dollop of ghee and a ladle of creamy tovve ( toor ) dal. I’d mix it thoroughly and make a well in the centre, into which my grandmother would spoon some fresh cream-laced curd. From breakfast to dinner, and dessert to round it off, dals hold an important position. Cutting across economic and social divides, it unites, acting as a thickener when meat is too expensive, and blending beautifully with vegetables and greens. “ Dals have always been one of the building blocks of South Indian cuisine. They not only lent protein, but also provided flavour,” says food historian Rakesh Raghunathan. “Each one has a certain texture and body, and a different use. Boiled toor and moong go into sambar , ground urad in idli , dosa and vadai , channa dal can be boiled, ground, roasted or fried for use in kootu, payasam , or podis . Each dal is versatile.” And becoming an adult and moving away from home usually coincides with a renewed love for this staple. The five southern States grow and consume dal very differently. But the unifier is that it is a part of every meal. Intercropping with rice has meant there’s a predominance of pourable, scoopable preparations, while the varied regions and climates have dictated flavours. (The five States produce nearly 4 million tonnes of pulses annually, contributing to around 12% to 15% of India’s total pulse production.) For instance, Kerala and Karnataka often soften their dals with freshly grated coconut or coconut milk, but the other three turn to tamarind pulp, chillies and asafoetida for tangy heat. “Food was never about human sustenance alone,” says cookbook author and food writer Mallika Badrinath; it was more ‘circular’. Earlier, urad dal , for instance, was soaked whole for idli and dosa , because “the green-black skin would be set aside for the cattle”. Native wisdom also dictated dishes. In Tamil cooking, different dals were cooked in specific combinations to ensure gut health — when it was not a fad, adds Badrinath. In Karnataka, many of the indigenous communities have their own ways of cooking pulses. “This area is full of rain-fed lands, and dals and ragi are an integral part of the cultivation cycle and meal design,” says Vishalakshi Padmanabhan of Bengaluru-based Buffalo Back Collective, which works extensively with rural communities. “The Iruliga tribes routinely forage greens and tubers, and eat them with very specific combinations of dal . A certain bassaru [gravy] will only use avare bele [broad beans], another will only work with hurulikaalu [horse gram]. We are now trying to establish the bio-availability of these combinations using science.” This is similar to how the Mullu Kuruma and Kurichiya communities of Wayanad in Kerala combine green gram with tender colocasia leaves or wild amaranth. https://www.thehindu.com/food/features/s.body_zh: 订阅账户还可享受《Premium Stories》《Editorials》《Opinions》等更多内容。点击“订阅”即可解锁这些内容。在印度南部，即使是在交谈中，大米和豆类也常常被相提并论：泰米尔语称“arisi-paruppu”，卡纳达语称“akki-bele”，马拉雅拉姆语称“chorum-parippum”，泰卢固语称“pappu-annam”。我在成长过程中一直喜爱paruppu。从记事起，我的早餐就是热腾腾的大米，配上一勺酥油和一大勺香浓的tovve（toor）dal。我会把它们充分拌匀，在中间挖出一个凹槽，再由祖母舀入一些新鲜、带着奶油香气的凝乳。从早餐到晚餐，再到以甜点收尾，dal都占据着重要位置。它跨越经济和社会界线，将人们凝聚在一起；当肉类价格过高时，它还可以充当增稠料，与蔬菜和绿叶菜完美搭配。“dal一直都是南印度美食的基础组成部分之一。它们不仅提供蛋白质，也带来风味。”美食史学家Rakesh Raghunathan说。“每一种dal都有特定的口感和质地，也各有不同用途。煮熟的toor和moong可用于sambar，磨碎的urad可用于idli、dosa和vadai，channa dal可以煮熟、磨碎、烘烤或油炸，用于kootu、payasam或podis。每一种dal都有多种用途。”成年并离家生活，通常也会让人重新爱上这种主食。印度南部的五个邦种植和食用dal的方式各不相同，但它们都有餐餐必备这一共同点。dal与水稻间作，使可 poured、可舀食的菜肴占据主导，而各地区和气候的多样性则决定了不同的风味。（这五个邦每年生产近400万吨豆类，约占印度豆类总产量的12%至15%。）例如，喀拉拉邦和卡纳塔克邦常用新鲜刨碎的椰子或椰奶使dal变得柔和，而另外三个邦则使用罗望子果肉、辣椒和阿魏来增添酸辣风味。“食物从来不只是为了维持人的生命。”食谱作者兼美食作家Mallika Badrinath说，它更多的是一种“循环”。例如，早些时候，人们会把urad dal整粒浸泡，用来制作idli和dosa，因为“绿黑色的外皮会被留给牲畜”。本土智慧也影响着菜肴。在泰米尔烹饪中，不同的dal会以特定组合烹制，以确保肠道健康——Badrinath补充说，这并非一时风潮。在卡纳塔克邦，许多原住民群体都有自己烹饪豆类的方式。“这一地区到处是依靠雨水灌溉的土地，dal和ragi是耕作周期和膳食设计中不可分割的一部分。”总部位于班加罗尔的Buffalo Back Collective的Vishalakshi Padmanabhan说。该组织与农村社区开展广泛合作。“Iruliga部落通常会采集绿叶菜和块茎，并把它们与非常特定的dal组合一起食用。某种bassaru［酱汁］只会使用avare bele［蚕豆］，另一种则只搭配hurulikaalu［马豆］。我们目前正尝试用科学方法确定这些组合的生物可利用性。”这与印度喀拉拉邦Wayanad的Mullu Kuruma和Kurichiya族群将绿豆搭配嫩芋叶或野生苋菜的方式相似。评论必须使用英文，并以完整句子撰写。评论不得含有辱骂性或人身攻击内容。请遵守我们的社区评论准则。我们已迁移至新的评论平台。如果你已经是《The Hindu》的注册用户并已登录，可以继续参与我们的文章讨论。如果你没有账户，请注册并登录后发表评论。用户登录自己的账户后，可以在Vuukle上查看以前的评论

https://leadership.ng/petrol-imports-fal.summary: The regulator’s October 2026 fact sheet showed that imports by oil marketing companies and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited averaged 15 million litres per day in October, against 28.9 million litres in October 2025. Also, consumption, measured by volumes trucked out to the domestic market, was 46.5 million litres daily, down from 56.7 million litres a year earlier. Imports increased 47 per cent from 10.2 million litres daily in September, while consumption rose five per cent from 44.4 million litres.
https://leadership.ng/petrol-imports-fal.summary_zh: 监管机构2026年10月的事实清单显示，石油销售企业和尼日利亚国家石油有限公司的进口量在10月平均为每天1,500万升，而2025年10月为每天2,890万升。消费量以运往国内市场的卡车运输量计算，10月为每天4,650万升，低于一年前的每天5,670万升。进口量较9月每天1,020万升增长47%，消费量则较每天4,440万升增长5%。
https://leadership.ng/petrol-imports-fal.body: The regulator’s October 2026 fact sheet showed that imports by oil marketing companies and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited averaged 15 million litres per day in October, against 28.9 million litres in October 2025. Also, consumption, measured by volumes trucked out to the domestic market, was 46.5 million litres daily, down from 56.7 million litres a year earlier. However, both figures rose on a monthly basis. Imports increased 47 per cent from 10.2 million litres daily in September, while consumption rose five per cent from 44.4 million litres. Total petrol receipts rose 21 per cent in October to 46.9 million litres daily from 38.7 million litres in September. Domestic refineries supplied 31.9 million litres, up 12 per cent. Local refineries supplied about 68 per cent of receipts, against about 37 per cent in October 2025, when they provided 17.1 million litres of 46 million litres received. Supply remained below the 50 million litres per day demand benchmark and the 13-month average of 50.2 million litres. Imports were below their 13-month average of 18.8 million litres daily and well under the 52.1 million litres recorded in November 2025, the highest in the period. The fact sheet showed that consumption was 93 per cent of the benchmark and below the 13-month mean of 51 million litres. It peaked at 63.7 million litres daily in December 2025. The Authority said higher crude receipts at domestic refineries and strong local petrol supply from the Dangote refinery meant most of the petrol consumed in October was refined in Nigeria. It said this reduced reliance on imports, eased pressure on foreign exchange and improved supply security. The Dangote refinery produced 48.51 million litres of petrol daily and ran at 103.73 per cent of its 650,000 barrels per day capacity, down 2.25 percentage points from September. Of its petrol output, 31.89 million litres went to the domestic market and 20.18 million litres, or 42 per cent of production, was exported. It drew 3.56 million litres daily from stock, and closing petrol stock fell 37 per cent to 229.9 million litres. Crude receipts at domestic refineries rose 19 per cent to 0.736 million barrels per day. Imported crude to Dangote grew 39 per cent to 118.4 thousand barrels per day, lowering the local crude share to 83.9 per cent from 86.1 per cent. The Port Harcourt, Warri and Kaduna refineries were not producing. Among modular refineries, Edo ran at 114.89 per cent of capacity, WalterSmith at 58.10 per cent, Aradel at 30.93 per cent and OPAC at 24.86 per cent. Duport was shut down. The modular refineries supplied 0.68 million litres of diesel daily, about 4.9 per cent of the 14 million litres benchmark. Petrol stock cover fell to 21.8 days from 23.9 days in September, 8.2 days below the required 30-day threshold. Inland depots held 19.53 days and vessels offshore 2.28 days. LPG cover was lower at 14.8 days. Diesel cover was 43.9 days and aviation fuel 75.8 days, both above the threshold. Diesel supply nearly doubled, rising 93 per cent to 16.8 million litres daily from 8.7 million litres. Imports rose to 6.1 million litres from 0.6 million litres, and domestic supply grew 32 per cent to 10.7 million litres. Supply moved above the 14 million litres benchmark and consumption of 15.5 million litres. Aviation fuel supply fell 36 per cent to 2.1 million litres daily, below consumption of 2.8 million litres and the 3 million litres benchmark. It was the lowest since July 2026. The Dangote refinery produced 26.44 million litres of aviation fuel daily, with exports taking 84 per cent. The Authority noted that the stock cover figure includes export-bound Dangote stock of 199.7 million litres. Cooking gas (LPG) supply rose 11 per cent to 5.2 kilotonnes per day, with domestic sources providing 4.8 kilotonnes. Consumption was 5.0 kilotonnes. Average petrol pump prices across eight monitored states rose about three per cent to N1,416.75 per litre, at the lower end of the indicative range of N1,413.71 to N1,447.00. The lowest actual prices were below the indicative minimum in all eight states. Cooking gas retailed from N1,208 per kilogramme in Lagos to N1,600 in Bauchi. Maximum retail prices exceeded the indicative price in all eight states monitored. Dated Brent crude averaged $124.77 per barrel, up seven per cent from September. Gasoline free-on-board cost fell eight per cent to $1,141.38 per metric tonne. The naira traded at N1,338.54 to the dollar, up one per cent. Total wholesale gas supply averaged 4.95 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d) from January to October 2026. Domestic supply averaged 2.04 bcf/d, or 41.3 per cent, while supply to Nigeria LNG (NLNG) averaged 2.91 bcf/d, or 58.7 per cent. Supply peaked at 5.14 bcf/d in April and dipped to 4.723 bcf/d in July. In October it was 4.951 bcf/d, up 2.7 per cent on September, with domestic supply at 2.113 bcf/d and NLNG at 2.838 bcf/d. Gas-to-power rose 10 per cent to 0.571 bcf/d. LNG exports rose seven per cent to 52,721 metric tonnes per day, and pipeline exports via the West African Gas Pipeline rose 11 per cent to 0.149 bcf/d. Gas processing plants held 16.187 bcf/d of installed capacity across 47 plants and processed 8.401 bcf/d, an average utilisation of 51.90 per cent. Four of the seven major facilities ran above 80 per cent, led by Gbaran Ubie at 90.64 per cent. Three ran below 50 per cent, with OB/OB at 25.69 per cent and Utorogu at 29.41 per cent. Condensate production rose from 1.505 million barrels in January to 2.209 million barrels in October. The Obiafu-Obrikom-Oben (OB3) pipeline reached 100 per cent completion in October. The Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano pipeline stood at 84.27 per cent after being re-scoped to include additional ancillary works. The Odidi-Warri expansion was at 79.58 per cent, the Escravos-Odidi pipeline at 34.75 per cent and the Escravos-Lagos compressor project at 97.18 per cent. The Authority said steady receipts remain important for supply stability, with rebuilding stock buffers as the next priority. We’ve got the edge. 监管机构2026年10月的事实清单显示，石油营销公司和尼日利亚国家石油公司有限公司的进口量在10月平均为每日1500万升，而2025年10月为每日2890万升。此外，以运往国内市场的卡车装载量衡量的消费量降至每日4650万升，一年前为每日5670万升。不过，这两项数字均较上月上升。进口量较9月每日1020万升增长47%，消费量则较9月每日4440万升增长5%。10月汽油接收总量较9月每日3870万升增长21%，达到每日4690万升。国内炼油厂供应量为3190万升，增长12%。本土炼油厂提供了约68%的接收量，而2025年10月约为37%，当时4600万升接收量中有1710万升来自本土炼油厂。供应量仍低于每日5000万升的需求基准和13个月平均值5020万升。进口量低于其13个月平均值每日1880万升，也远低于2025年11月创下的5210万升，后者为该期间最高水平。事实清单显示，消费量达到基准的93%，低于13个月平均值5100万升。消费量在2025年12月达到峰值，每日6370万升。管理局表示，国内炼油厂原油接收量增加，加上Dangote炼油厂汽油供应强劲，意味着10月消费的大部分汽油均在尼日利亚炼制。这降低了对进口的依赖，缓解了外汇压力，并提高了供应安全性。Dangote炼油厂每日生产汽油4851万升，产能利用率为每日65万桶产能的103.73%，较9月下降2.25个百分点。在汽油产量中，3189万升供应国内市场，另有2018万升、即产量的42%用于出口。该厂每日从库存中提取356万升汽油，期末汽油库存下降37%至2.299亿升。国内炼油厂原油接收量增长19%，达到每日73.6万桶。运往Dangote炼油厂的进口原油增长39%，达到每日11.84万桶，使本地原油占比从86.1%降至83.9%。Port Harcourt、Warri和Kaduna炼油厂没有生产。在模块化炼油厂中，Edo炼油厂的产能利用率为114.89%，WalterSmith为58.10%，Aradel为30.93%，OPAC为24.86%。Duport处于停产状态。模块化炼油厂每日供应68万升柴油，约占1400万升基准的4.9%。汽油库存覆盖期从9月的23.9天降至21.8天，比规定的30天门槛低8.2天。内陆油库可维持19.53天供应，近海船只上的库存可维持2.28天。LPG库存覆盖期较低，仅为14.8天。柴油库存覆盖期为43.9天，航空燃料为75.8天，两者均高于门槛。柴油供应量几乎翻倍，从每日870万升增长93%至每日1680万升。进口量从60万升增至610万升，国内供应量增长32%，达到每日1070万升。供应量超过1400万升的基准和1550万升的消费量。航空燃料供应量下降36%，降至每日210万升，低于每日280万升的消费量和300万升的基准。这是2026年7月以来的最低水平。Dangote炼油厂每日生产航空燃料2644万升，其中84%用于出口。管理局指出，库存覆盖期数据包括Dangote炼油厂199.7万升、拟出口的库存。液化石油气（LPG）供应量增长11%，达到每日5200吨，其中国内来源提供4800吨。消费量为5000吨。8个受监测州的汽油平均泵价上涨约3%，达到每升N1,416.75，处于N1,413.71至N1,447.00的指示价格区间低端。这8个州的实际最低价格均低于指示价格下限。液化石油气零售价从拉各斯每公斤N1,208到包奇每公斤N1,600。所有8个受监测州的最高零售价均超过指示价格。基准日Brent原油均价为每桶124.77美元，较9月上涨7%。汽油离岸成本下降8%，降至每公吨1,141.38美元。奈拉兑美元汇率上涨1%，至N1,338.54。2026年1月至10月，天然气批发供应总量平均为每日49.5亿立方英尺（bcf/d）。国内供应平均为每日2.04 He believes this culture has made Silicon Valley a hotbed for innovation and encouraged more young Americans to pursue their own entrepreneurial ventures. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/lifestyle/p.summary_zh: 李表示，与韩国不同，硅谷非常看重实践经验，尤其是在初创企业工作的经验。他认为，这种文化使硅谷成为创新热土，并鼓励更多年轻美国人投身自己的创业事业。7月，Philyron 获得了 Andreessen Horowitz 的50万美元投资。该机构又称 a16z，是硅谷最强大、最有声望的风险投资机构之一。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/lifestyle/p.body: Lee Seung-heon, also known as Heon Lee in the U.S., has chosen a path that many other Koreans would consider too risky to take. He dropped out of college to work full time at Philyron, a San Francisco-based maritime technology startup he co-founded in June this year. “Korean students and their parents feel pressure when it comes to choosing a career over a college education. But in Silicon Valley, I’ve met plenty of young Americans who dropped out of prestigious universities to start their own businesses,” he told The Korea Times. “There is certainly a cultural difference between the two countries when it comes to college education. I concluded that starting my own business was the right decision and that spending three more years in college would be meaningless because schools don’t teach you how to start a business and keep it growing.” Lee, 24, initially studied political science at Boston University. After completing his freshman year, he transferred to the University of Michigan at Ann Arbor before returning to Korea to fulfill his mandatory military service. Initially, he planned to return to school to study computer science and political science, but he changed his mind. Lee saw enormous opportunities in two simultaneous booms: the rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) and the thriving U.S. shipbuilding industry. He decided to seize the opportunities created by these emerging trends. In the U.S., particularly in the information technology industry, dropping out of college is not considered taboo. This may be partly because several tech billionaires left university to build their businesses. Bill Gates dropped out of Harvard University and co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen. Steve Jobs dropped out of Reed College and co-founded Apple. Mark Zuckerberg, Michael Dell and Dustin Moskovitz are among other prominent college dropouts. Unlike in Korea, Lee said, real world experience, particularly experience working at startups, is highly valued in Silicon Valley. He believes this culture has made Silicon Valley a hotbed for innovation and encouraged more young Americans to pursue their own entrepreneurial ventures. Philyron develops AI-driven thermal and acoustic sensors that can be installed on ship hulls to provide operators with critical information about the condition and lifecycle of onboard devices and equipment, including when they need to be repaired or replaced. The technology makes vessel maintenance more predictable and helps operators manage their fleets more efficiently. After San Francisco Bay Ferry became Philyron’s first customer, several other U.S. government agencies also adopted the startup’s sensors. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration is among the company’s government partners. “Like other Korean parents, my parents initially didn't approve of my decision to leave college. But they have changed their minds after seeing the progress my business has made. Now they encourage me to keep doing whatever I want,” he said. In July, Philyron secured $500,000 in investment from Andreessen Horowitz, also known as a16z, one of the most powerful and prestigious Silicon Valley venture capital firms. Since then, Lee’s maritime startup has continued to expand its partnerships, primarily with U.S. government agencies. “At Philyron, we are a small team of four, including myself. We aim to reach the $1 million revenue milestone next year,” he said. “Currently, most of our clients are U.S. government agencies. We’d like to sell our products to defense operators.” Lee wears two hats at Philyron, keeping him busy. Like the company's other engineers, he works on software development. At the same time, he actively reaches out to potential clients to market the company's products. He said his network of industry insiders had played an important role in helping him secure contracts with U.S. government agencies. Among those who have supported him is Kevin Humphreys, a vice president at Saronic Technologies. “Mr. Humphreys saw opportunities in our startup and invested in it. Currently, we provide our sensors mainly to vessels, but they can also be used in other types of vehicles, such as trucks and aircraft. Mr. Humphreys recognized this potential,” he said. As a co-founder, Lee said his ambition was relatively modest: to keep growing the business and build a sustainable company. “All of our staff members are smart and talented. They are all students at Stanford, MIT and Berkeley, and they work part time,” he said. “I’d like to have them join us full time. To make that happen, I need to prove that this company is financially viable enough to convince them to put their college education on hold and work here full time.”
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/lifestyle/p.title_zh: 一名24岁韩国人的硅谷豪赌获得a16z支持，迎来回报
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/lifestyle/p.body_zh:
李承勋（在美国也被称为Heon Lee）选择了许多其他韩国人认为风险太大的道路。他从大学退学，全职供职于Philyron——这是一家总部位于旧金山的海事科技初创企业，由他于今年6月共同创办。

他告诉《韩国时报》：“韩国学生及其父母在选择职业生涯还是大学教育时都会感到压力。但在硅谷，我遇到了许多放弃名校大学学业、创办自己企业的年轻美国人。”

“在大学教育方面，两国之间确实存在文化差异。我得出结论，创办自己的企业才是正确的决定；再花三年读大学毫无意义，因为学校不会教你如何创办并持续发展企业。”

现年24岁的李最初在波士顿大学学习政治学。大一结束后，他转入密歇根大学安娜堡分校，随后返回韩国服义务兵役。起初，他打算复学并学习计算机科学和政治学，但后来改变了主意。李看到两股同时兴起的热潮蕴含着巨大机遇：人工智能（AI）的快速增长，以及美国造船业的蓬勃发展。他决定抓住这些新兴趋势带来的机会。

在美国，尤其是在信息技术行业，从大学退学并不被视为禁忌。这或许是因为有多位科技亿万富翁离开大学创业。比尔·盖茨从哈佛大学退学，与保罗·艾伦共同创办了微软。史蒂夫·乔布斯从里德学院退学，共同创办了苹果公司。马克·扎克伯格、迈克尔·戴尔和达斯廷·莫斯科维茨也是其他著名的大学退学者。李说，与韩国不同，在硅谷，真实-world经验，尤其是初创企业工作经验，受到高度重视。他认为，这种文化使硅谷成为创新熱土，也鼓励更多年轻美国人 pursue自己的创业事业。

Philyron研发由人工智能驱动的热学与声学传感器，可安装在船体上，为运营方提供有关船上设备和器材状况及生命周期的重要信息，包括何时需要维修或更换。这项技术使船舶维护更具可预测性，帮助运营方更高效地管理船队。

在San Francisco Bay Ferry成为Philyron的首位客户后，美国多家政府机构也开始采用这家初创企业的传感器。美国国家海洋和大气管理局是该公司的政府合作伙伴之一。

他说：“和其他韩国父母一样，我父母最初不赞成我离开大学的决定。但看到我的企业取得进展后，他们改变了看法。现在，他们鼓励我继续做任何想做的事。”

7月，Philyron获得了Andreessen Horowitz（又称a16z）的50万美元投资。该公司是硅谷最强劲、最有声望的风险投资机构之一。此后，李这家海事初创企业继续扩大合作范围，主要合作方是美国政府机构。

他说：“在Philyron，我们是一个四人小团队，包括我本人在内。我们的目标是明年达到100万美元的营收里程碑。目前，大多数客户是美国政府机构。我们希望向国防领域的运营方销售产品。”

在Philyron，李身兼两职，忙个不停。与公司的其他工程师一样，他负责软件开发。与此同时，他积极联系潜在客户，推广公司的产品。他说，自己在业内人士中建立的人脉网络，在帮助他拿下美国政府机构合同方面发挥了重要作用。

支持他的人士中包括Saronic Technologies副总裁Kevin Humphreys。他说：“Humphreys先生看到了我们初创企业的机遇，并为其投资。目前，我们主要向船舶提供传感器，但传感器也可用于其他类型的交通工具，如卡车和飞机。Humphreys先生认识到了这种潜力。”

作为共同创始人，李说自己的抱负相对 modest：继续推动业务增长，打造一家可持续经营的企业。

他说：“我们所有员工都很聪明、很有才华。他们都是斯坦福大学、MIT和伯克利的学生，目前兼职工作。我希望他们全职加入我们。要实现这一点，我需要证明这家公司在财务上足够稳健，足以说服他们暂缓大学学业，到这里全职工作。”

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/why-.summary: The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (rtd), has reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to a comprehensive, whole-of-government strategy to combat terrorism, while seeking stronger security cooperation with the European Union (EU). https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/why-.summary_zh: 国防部长Christopher Gwabin Musa将军（退役）重申，联邦政府致力于采取全面且政府各部委协同的战略打击恐怖主义，同时寻求与欧洲联盟（EU）加强安全合作。Musa在比利时布鲁塞尔欧洲议会举行的第三届舒曼安全与防务论坛上透露了上述立场，并代表尼日利亚出席活动。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/why-.body: The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (rtd), has reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to a comprehensive, whole-of-government strategy to combat terrorism, while seeking stronger security cooperation with the European Union (EU). Musa made this known at the third edition of the Schuman Security and Defence Forum held at the European Parliament in Brussels, Belgium, where he represented Nigeria. A statement issued by the Special Adviser on Media to the Minister, Leah Katung-Babatunde quoted the minister saying Nigeria was shifting from a predominantly military approach to a coordinated counterterrorism strategy involving intelligence gathering, law enforcement, community engagement and socio-economic interventions. He explained that terrorism remained a complex security challenge fuelled by economic vulnerabilities, porous borders, local grievances and transnational organised crime. The minister said the strategy, guided by Nigeria’s National Counter Terrorism Strategy (NACTEST), reflected the administration’s determination to address both the immediate threats posed by terrorist groups and the underlying factors sustaining insecurity. Addressing the growing use of emerging technologies by violent extremist groups, Musa highlighted Nigeria’s efforts to counter the illicit deployment of drones, digital communication devices and satellite technologies. He said the Armed Forces of Nigeria were deploying intelligence-led operations, advanced surveillance systems, unmanned aerial platforms and military artificial intelligence to weaken terrorist networks. He particularly disclosed that troops of Operation Hadin Kai intercepted more than 400 Starlink communication devices linked to terrorist networks in the North-East in May 2026. Musa also highlighted the Ministry of Defence’s efforts to promote indigenous defence innovation through research and partnerships with the private sector. He called for stronger collaboration with the European Union in counter-drone technologies, digital forensics and satellite intelligence to enhance Nigeria’s capacity to respond to evolving security threats. On the financial networks sustaining terrorism, the minister stressed the need to dismantle criminal economies, including kidnapping for ransom, illegal mining, cattle rustling and illicit arms trafficking. He said the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU), National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC) and other security agencies were working together to trace illicit financial flows, prosecute criminal facilitators and strengthen border security to disrupt terrorist supply chains. He also emphasised that the Armed Forces remained committed to operating within the framework of national laws and international humanitarian law, with priority given to civilian protection and due process in the prosecution of suspects. According to him, Nigeria also recognises the importance of rehabilitation and reintegration programmes for eligible former combatants through initiatives such as Operation Safe Corridor. The Schuman Security and Defence Forum provides a platform for high-level discussions on international peace, security and defence among defence ministers of partner countries, European Union member states, representatives of international organisations and leading think tanks. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/why-.title_zh: 尼日利亚为何寻求加强与欧盟的伙伴关系，以打击恐怖主义
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/why-.body_zh: 国防部长兼退役上将Christopher Gwabin Musa再次强调，联邦政府致力于采取全面、全政府协同战略打击恐怖主义，同时寻求与欧洲联盟（EU）加强安全合作。Musa在比利时布鲁塞尔欧洲议会举行的第三届舒曼安全与防务论坛上宣布了上述表态，并代表尼日利亚发言。部长媒体特别顾问Leah Katung-Babatunde发表的一份声明援引部长的话说，尼日利亚正从主要依靠军事手段转向协调一致的反恐战略，综合开展情报收集、执法、社区参与和社会经济干预。他解释道，恐怖主义仍是一项复杂的安全挑战，其推动因素包括经济脆弱性、边境管控松散、地方矛盾和跨国有组织犯罪。部长表示，这项以尼日利亚国家反恐战略（NACTEST）为指导的战略，体现了政府决心既应对恐怖组织造成的直接威胁，也处理持续滋生不安全局势的根本因素。针对暴力极端组织日益频繁地使用新兴技术，Musa强调尼日利亚正在努力打击无人机、数字通信设备和卫星技术的非法使用。他说，尼日利亚武装部队正部署以情报为引导的行动、先进监视系统、无人平台和军事人工智能，以削弱恐怖组织网络。他特别披露，2026年5月，Hadin Kai行动部队在东北部截获了400多台与恐怖组织网络有关的Starlink通信设备。Musa还强调，国防部正通过研究以及与私营部门建立伙伴关系，推动本土国防创新。他呼吁与欧洲联盟在反无人机技术、数字取证和卫星情报方面加强协作，以提升尼日利亚应对不断演变的安全威胁的能力。谈及为恐怖主义提供支撑的金融网络，部长强调必须摧毁犯罪经济，包括绑架勒索、非法采矿、盗掠牲畜和非法武器贩运。他说，尼日利亚金融情报单位（NFIU）、国家反恐中心（NCTC）及其他安全机构正协同追查非法资金流、起诉犯罪协助者并加强边境安全，以切断恐怖组织的供应链。他还强调，尼日利亚武装部队仍致力于在本国法律和国际人道法框架内行动，并优先保护平民，在起诉嫌疑人时保障正当程序。他表示，尼日利亚也认识到，通过“安全走廊行动”等举措，为符合条件的原战斗人员实施康复和重新融入计划具有重要意义。舒曼安全与防务论坛为合作伙伴国家国防部长、欧洲联盟成员国、国际组织代表和主要智库就国际和平、安全与防务问题进行高级别讨论提供平台。本文所载评论不代表Vanguard报纸及其任何员工的观点。

Unlock these with Subscription India's position on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) is "very clear" and there has been "absolutely no change" in it, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Friday (November 20, 2026), amid a visit by Pakistan Minister Musadik Malik to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi. Mr. Malik, who arrived here in the early hours of Friday (November 20, 2026), attended the opening day of the three-day forum in the evening. The event, being hosted by India at the historic Purana Quila, was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. India had announced on October 28 that invitations had been extended to all SCO members, including Pakistan, in keeping with established practice. It was perhaps the first time New Delhi had invited a Pakistani minister to attend an event in India since the May 7-10 military hostilities last year following Operation Sindoor. Pakistan had announced on November 14 that its Climate Change Minister Malik would participate in the forum. At his bi-weekly media briefing, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal was asked how New Delhi viewed Mr. Malik's participation in the India-hosted forum, given that he does not hold the culture portfolio and had reportedly made comments on the IWT. "As far as IWT is concerned, we have made our position very clear, and that is where it remains. There is absolutely no change," Mr. Jaiswal said. India suspended the treaty in 2025 as one of the punitive measures against Pakistan after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack last year that claimed 26 lives. Mr. Malik's participation in the forum is being seen by some experts as an opportunity in a multilateral framework that may help improve ties between the two neighbours. Interacting with reporters on the sidelines of the forum, Mr. Malik, when asked about the role of culture in fostering better ties between India and Pakistan, said, "Culture has a very key role to play". Hours before the inauguration, the MEA on Friday (November 20, 2026) said the forum was a "multilateral event within the SCO framework", for which invitations had been extended to all members of the grouping, including Pakistan. "India is hosting the 1st SCO Civilisation Dialogue on 20-22 November 2026, in New Delhi. This is a multilateral event within the SCO framework, for which invitations have been extended to all members of the SCO, including Pakistan," the MEA said in a post on X. "Observers and Dialogue Partners of the SCO have also been invited to attend the Dialogue, which will be inaugurated this evening by the Hon’ble Prime Minister," it said. The event is being hosted by the Ministry of Culture and the MEA. The SCO was founded at a summit in Shanghai in 2001 by the presidents of Russia, China, the Kyrgyz Republic, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/i.body_zh:

印度外交部周五（2026年11月20日）表示，印度对《印度河水条约》（IWT）的立场“非常明确”，并且“绝对没有任何改变”。此前，巴基斯坦部长穆萨迪克·马利克到访新德里，参加上海合作组织文明对话论坛。马利克先生于周五（2026年11月20日）凌晨抵达印度，当晚出席了这为期三天论坛的开幕日活动。此次活动在历史悠久的浦拉纳堡由印度主办，总理纳伦德拉·莫迪主持开幕。

印度曾于10月28日宣布，按照既定惯例，已向包括巴基斯坦在内的所有上海合作组织成员国发出邀请。这或许是去年5月7日至10日“辛杜尔行动”引发军事冲突后，新德里首次邀请巴基斯坦部长赴印度参加活动。

巴基斯坦于11月14日宣布，其气候变化部长马利克将参加该论坛。在每两周举行一次的媒体吹风会上，印度外交部（MEA）发言人兰迪尔·贾伊瓦尔被问及，鉴于马利克先生并不主管文化事务，且据报道曾就《印度河水条约》发表评论，新德里如何看待他参加印度主办的论坛。

贾伊瓦尔先生说：“就《印度河水条约》而言，我们已经非常明确地表明了立场，而且立场依然如旧。绝对没有任何改变。”

去年4月22日帕哈尔加姆恐怖袭击造成26人死亡后，印度于2025年暂停履行该条约，以此作为针对巴基斯坦的惩罚措施之一。

一些专家认为，马利克先生参加论坛提供了一个多边框架下的机会，可能有助于改善这两个邻国之间的关系。在论坛场边与记者互动时，当被问及文化在促进印巴关系方面发挥的作用时，马利克先生说：“文化发挥着非常关键的作用。”

开幕前数小时，印度外交部于周五（2026年11月20日）表示，该论坛是“上海合作组织框架内的一场多边活动”，已向包括巴基斯坦在内的该组织所有成员发出邀请。

印度外交部在X平台上发帖称：“印度于2026年11月20日至22日在新德里举办首届上海合作组织文明对话。这是上海合作组织框架内的一场多边活动，我们已向包括巴基斯坦在内的上海合作组织全体成员发出邀请。”

该帖还说：“上海合作组织的观察员国和对话伙伴也受邀出席对话活动，活动将于今晚由尊敬的总理主持开幕。”

本次活动由印度文化部和外交部共同主办。

上海合作组织于2001年在上海举行的一次峰会上成立，创始成员为俄罗斯、中国、吉尔吉斯共和国、哈萨克斯坦、塔吉克斯坦和乌兹别克斯坦的总统。印度和巴基斯坦于2017年成为该组织的永久成员。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/21/c.summary: Nigeria’s push to expand gas-powered mobility is gaining momentum as the federal government’s removal of VAT and import duties on CNG vehicles, conversion kits, and related equipment begins to reshape the economics of transportation. For Nigeria’s transport operators, the cost of fuel is only one part of the equation. Nigeria’s transition to CNG is happening against the backdrop of a transport sector already under pressure from high vehicle operating costs, inadequate infrastructure and expensive maintenance.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/21/c.summary_zh: 随着联邦政府取消压缩天然气汽车、改装套件及相关设备的增值税和进口关税，尼日利亚（国家，首都阿布贾）推动燃气交通发展的势头日益增强，并开始重塑交通运输的经济成本。对尼日利亚的运输运营商而言，燃料成本只是其中一个考量因素。尼日利亚向压缩天然气交通转型之际，交通运输业正面临车辆运营成本高、基础设施不足和维护费用昂贵等压力。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/21/c.body: Nigeria’s push to expand gas-powered mobility is gaining momentum as the federal government’s removal of VAT and import duties on CNG vehicles, conversion kits, and related equipment begins to reshape the economics of transportation. The incentives could lower entry costs for motorists and fleet operators while creating fresh opportunities across the automotive value chain, but their long-term impact will depend on infrastructure, financing, and reliable gas supply. For Nigeria’s transport operators, the cost of fuel is only one part of the equation. The price of acquiring a vehicle, converting it to an alternative fuel, sourcing spare parts, maintaining the powertrain, and keeping vehicles on the road all determine whether a cheaper fuel ultimately translates into cheaper mobility. This is where the federal government’s decision to remove Value Added Tax (VAT) and import duties on Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) and related equipment becomes significant beyond the energy sector. Although the incentives were introduced to make gas more accessible and encourage investment, their implications are increasingly being felt in transportation, particularly as Nigeria seeks to expand CNG-powered mobility. For an industry grappling with high operating costs, the removal of taxes on CNG equipment and conversion components could lower some of the financial barriers facing motorists and commercial transport operators seeking alternatives to petrol and diesel. The journey towards the tax exemptions gained momentum in 2023 when the Nigeria Liquefied and Compressed Gases Association (NLCGA) took its concerns to the presidency through an advocacy engagement with Olu Verheijen, Special Adviser to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Energy. The association highlighted the pressure created by VAT and import duties on LPG, CNG and the equipment required to store, transport, distribute and use gas. For the mobility sector, the issue was particularly important because CNG adoption depends on more than the availability of natural gas. It requires conversion kits, cylinders, valves, dispensers, compressors, trucks, safety equipment and other components. When these items attract additional taxes and duties, the cost is eventually reflected in the investment required by operators and, potentially, the price paid by vehicle owners. The NLCGA subsequently submitted detailed proposals outlining areas requiring government intervention and also called for stronger coordination among government agencies responsible for policies affecting the gas industry. The engagements that followed with the Office of the Special Adviser and the Federal Ministry of Finance eventually produced policy measures aimed at reducing some of those costs. On November 28, 2023, the government provided for zero import duty and VAT on LPG and a range of essential equipment. The relief covered items such as gas cylinders, cascades, leak detectors, pipes, valves, dispensers, generators and LPG trucks. A subsequent directive in December extended similar treatment to CNG equipment, strengthening the fiscal framework around the emerging gas-for-mobility market. The economics of CNG conversion are relatively straightforward. A vehicle owner considering conversion must weigh the initial cost against the expected savings from using CNG. If the equipment, installation, and related components become more expensive because of taxes and import duties, the period required to recover the investment becomes longer. That can discourage private motorists and commercial operators from making the switch. The removal of VAT and import duties, therefore, has the potential to reduce the upfront cost of conversion and improve the business case for CNG. For a commercial bus, taxi, haulage truck or delivery vehicle that operates for several hours every day, fuel represents a significant proportion of operating expenditure. An alternative fuel becomes attractive when the cost of conversion and the availability of refueling infrastructure are also manageable. The fiscal incentives seek to address part of that equation. They also have implications for companies importing fully CNG-powered vehicles. By removing applicable import duty and VAT on qualifying vehicles and equipment, the government is creating an additional incentive for businesses to consider gas-powered fleets. For Ladi Falola, President of the Nigeria Liquefied and Compressed Gases Association (NLCGA), the tax incentives should be viewed as part of a broader effort to build a viable gas market rather than simply as measures for reducing government revenue. Falola said reducing the fiscal burden on CNG equipment could encourage investment and make the transition to gas-powered transportation more attractive to motorists and fleet operators. He stressed, however, that tax relief alone would not deliver the desired transformation. The NLCGA President also sees the development of the CNG market as an opportunity to deepen activity across the domestic automotive and gas value chains, particularly through local assembly, technical services and equipment supply. Nigeria’s CNG transition has increasingly moved from policy announcements to fleet-level decisions. Large commercial operators are exploring the technology as they seek to contain fuel expenditure and reduce exposure to petrol and diesel price volatility. Dangote Cement, for instance, has announced plans to transition substantial portions of its fleet to CNG-powered vehicles. For businesses operating hundreds or thousands of vehicles, the economics can be compelling. A reduction in fuel expenditure multiplied across a large fleet can produce significant savings. But those savings can only materialise if vehicles have reliable access to CNG. This makes the tax exemptions part of a much larger mobility equation. Lower conversion costs without adequate refuelling stations could leave vehicles underutilised. More filling stations without sufficient demand could undermine investment returns. And cheaper conversion equipment without adequate standards and trained technicians could create safety and reliability concerns. The policy, therefore, needs to be viewed as one component of a developing CNG ecosystem rather than a standalone solution. Nigeria’s transition to CNG is happening against the backdrop of a transport sector already under pressure from high vehicle operating costs, inadequate infrastructure and expensive maintenance. The emergence of CNG creates an opportunity to reshape some of those economics, but it also exposes infrastructure gaps. CNG vehicles require appropriate compression, storage and dispensing infrastructure. Conversion centres need trained personnel and equipment. Spare parts must be readily available. Vehicle owners also need confidence that they can refuel without making significant detours or facing prolonged queues. This is where the removal of taxes on equipment could have a wider impact. Lower import costs can make it easier for investors to acquire the equipment needed to establish and expand CNG infrastructure. As more operators enter the market, competition could improve availability and service delivery. The objective should, therefore, go beyond getting more vehicles converted. It should be to build a functioning market around those vehicles. The CNG policy also fits into the Government’s broader attempt to diversify Nigeria’s transportation fuel mix. For decades, petrol and diesel have dominated road transportation, leaving motorists highly exposed to changes in fuel prices and supply conditions. CNG offers another option, particularly for high-mileage commercial vehicles. But the transition cannot be sustained by tax exemptions alone. The industry still needs consistent policies, investment in refuelling infrastructure, reliable gas supply, standards enforcement,nt and affordable financing for vehicle conversion. Even where the cost of conversion falls, many commercial drivers and small fleet operators may still struggle to raise the capital required to convert their vehicles. Access to credit, leasing arrangements and fleet financing could therefore determine how widely the technology spreads beyond large corporations. The development of local manufacturing and assembly of conversion equipment could also become increasingly important. If Nigeria eventually produces a larger proportion of the equipment required by the CNG market locally, the country could reduce its dependence on imported components while creating opportunities for manufacturers, technicians and other businesses within the automotive value chain. The implications of the tax policy extend beyond motorists. A growing CNG market creates opportunities for vehicle dealers, conversion centres, component suppliers, mechanics, engineers, transport companies and energy businesses. As more vehicles move towards gas, demand will grow for specialised maintenance and technical services. This could produce a new layer of expertise within Nigeria’s automotive industry. Workshops that traditionally focused on petrol and diesel vehicles will increasingly need technicians trained to work safely on CNG systems. Parts distributors will need to understand the requirements of gas-powered vehicles. Insurance and inspection businesses will also have to adapt to a changing vehicle population. In this sense, the CNG transition could become an industrial policy as much as a fuel policy. The more equipment and services that can be produced and supplied locally, the greater the potential economic benefit beyond fuel savings. The NLCGA has set an ambition of increasing annual LPG consumption to five million metric tons by 2030 while supporting wider adoption of gas in transportation. The government’s tax exemptions provide an important starting point by reducing some of the costs associated with importing gas and mobility equipment. But their ultimate success will depend on whether the benefits translate into lower acquisition costs, more investment and greater consumer access. For investors, the question is whether Nigeria can create a market large and stable enough to justify investment in infrastructure and equipment. For government, the challenge is ensuring that fiscal incentives are supported by the policies and infrastructure needed to make the transition work. What began as an industry advocacy effort in 2023 has evolved into a policy intervention with implications for Nigeria’s automotive and transport sectors. The removal of VAT and import duties does not, by itself, guarantee cheaper mobility. Fuel prices, exchange rates, gas availability, infrastructure, vehicle costs, and maintenance will continue to influence the economics of transportation. But by removing some of the fiscal costs attached to CNG equipment and vehicles, the Government has lowered one barrier to adoption. If investment in refueling infrastructure keeps pace with vehicle conversions, technical standards remain strong, financing becomes accessible and supply remains reliable, CNG could move beyond being an alternative fuel promoted through government policy to become a commercially viable component of Nigeria’s transport system. For a country searching for ways to reduce the cost of mobility while developing its domestic gas resources, that distinction matters. The real measure of the VAT and import-duty exemptions, therefore, will not be the taxes the government has removed. It will be the vehicles that are converted, the filling stations that are built, the businesses that emerge and, ultimately, the extent to which Nigerian motorists can move people and goods at lower and more predictable cost. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/21/c.title_zh: 压缩天然气税收减免：为尼日利亚交通运输业注入动力
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/21/c.body_zh:
尼日利亚推动扩大燃气交通的动力日益增强。随着联邦政府取消压缩天然气汽车、改装套件及相关设备的增值税和进口关税，交通运输的经济格局开始发生改变。这些激励措施可降低驾车者和车队运营商的入门成本，同时为汽车产业链带来新的机遇，但其长期影响将取决于基础设施、融资以及可靠的天然气供应。

对尼日利亚运输运营商而言，燃油成本只是整个经济账本的一部分。购置车辆、将其改装为使用替代燃料、采购备件、维护动力系统以及确保车辆持续运行的成本，共同决定廉价燃料最终能否转化为更低的出行成本。正是在这一背景下，联邦政府决定取消液化石油气（LPG）、压缩天然气（CNG）及相关设备的增值税和进口关税，其意义超出了能源行业本身。尽管这些激励措施旨在提高燃气可获得性并鼓励投资，但随着尼日利亚寻求扩大压缩天然气动力交通，其影响正日益在交通运输领域显现。

对于一个承受高运营成本压力的行业，取消压缩天然气设备和改装部件的税收可降低部分财务门槛，帮助驾车者和商业运输运营商寻找汽油和柴油的替代方案。争取税收减免的进程在2023年获得推动。当时，尼日利亚液化气和压缩气体协会（NLCGA）通过与总统博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布的能源特别顾问奥卢·弗尔海恩开展倡导活动，将相关担忧提交给总统府。该协会强调，增值税和进口关税对LPG、CNG以及储存、运输、分配和使用燃气所需设备造成了压力。

对交通出行领域而言，这一问题尤为重要，因为采用压缩天然气不仅取决于天然气供应，还依赖改装套件、气瓶、阀门、加油设备、压缩机、卡车、安全设备及其他部件。如果这些物品被额外征收税款和关税，成本最终会反映在运营商所需投资中，并可能转嫁给车主。NLCGA随后提交了详细建议，列出需要政府干预的领域，同时呼吁负责影响燃气行业政策的各政府机构加强协调。此后，与特别顾问办公室和联邦财政部的沟通促成了一系列旨在降低部分成本的政策措施。

2023年11月28日，政府规定LPG及一系列必要设备的进口关税和增值税均为零。减免范围包括燃气瓶、级联式储气装置、泄漏探测器、管道、阀门、加油设备、发电机和LPG运输车等。12月发布的另一项指令将类似待遇扩大至CNG设备，为新兴的燃气出行市场巩固了财政政策框架。

压缩天然气改装的经济账目相对简单。考虑改装车辆的车主必须将初始成本与使用CNG预计节省的费用进行权衡。如果设备、安装和相关部件因税收及进口关税而变得更昂贵，投资回收期就会延长。这可能打消私人车主和商业运营商转用压缩天然气的意愿。因此，取消增值税和进口关税有望降低改装的前期成本，并改善CNG的商业可行性。

对于每天运行数小时的商用客车、出租车、货运卡车或配送车辆，燃油占运营支出的很大比例。当改装成本可控且加气基础设施供应充足时，替代燃料便具有吸引力。财政激励措施旨在解决这一经济账目中的一部分问题。这些措施也对进口全CNG动力车辆的企业产生影响。通过取消符合条件的车辆和设备所适用的进口关税及增值税，政府为企业考虑采用燃气车队提供了额外激励。

尼日利亚液化气和压缩气体协会（NLCGA）会长拉迪·法洛拉认为，这些税收激励应被视为建设可持续燃气市场这一更广泛努力的一部分，而不应仅仅被看作减少政府收入的措施。法洛拉表示，降低CNG设备的财政负担可鼓励投资，并使驾车者和车队运营商更愿意转向燃气运输。不过，他强调，仅靠税收减免无法带来预期中的转型。NLCGA会长还认为，CNG市场的发展为深化国内汽车和燃气产业链活动提供了机会，尤其是通过本地组装、技术服务和设备供应来实现。

尼日利亚向CNG的转型正日益从政策宣布落实到车队层面的实际决策。大型商业运营商正在探索这项技术，以控制燃油支出并降低对汽油和柴油价格波动的暴露。例如， Dangote Cement已宣布计划将车队中相当一部分车辆转为CNG动力。对于运营数百或数千辆车的企业而言，其经济收益可能十分可观。车队规模越大，燃油支出的降幅乘以车辆数量，节省金额也就越可观。但只有车辆能够稳定获得CNG供应，这些节省才能实现。因此，税收减免只是整个出行经济体系中更大一环。

如果降低改装成本却没有充足的加气站，车辆利用率可能仍然偏低。如果加气站增加而需求不足，投资回报又可能受损。如果改装设备价格下降，却缺乏完善标准和训练有素的技术人员，则可能引发安全和可靠性问题。因此，这项政策应被视为正在形成的CNG生态系统的一个组成部分，而非一项独立解决方案。

尼日利亚正在向CNG转型，而其交通行业同时面临车辆运营成本高、基础设施不足和维护费用昂贵等压力。CNG的兴起为重塑部分成本结构提供了机会，但也暴露了基础设施缺口。CNG车辆需要配套的压缩、储存和加气基础设施，改装中心需要训练有素的人员和设备，备件必须能够随时供应。车主还需要相信，他们无需大幅绕行或长时间排队就能完成加油。正是在这一背景下，取消设备税收可能产生更广泛影响。较低的进口成本可让投资者更容易购建设立和扩建CNG基础设施所需的设备。随着更多运营商进入市场，竞争或许能改善设备供应和服务质量。因此，政策目标不应止于让更多车辆完成改装，而应着眼于围绕这些车辆建立运转良好的市场。

CNG政策也是政府推动尼日利亚交通燃料结构多元化总体努力的一部分。数十年来，汽油和柴油一直主导道路运输，使驾车者高度暴露于燃料价格和供应条件的变化之下。CNG提供了另一种选择，尤其适合高里程商业车辆。但这一转型不能仅靠税收减免维系。行业仍需要稳定的政策、对加气基础设施的投资、可靠的燃气供应、标准执行，以及可负担的车辆改装融资。即使改装成本下降，许多商业驾驶者和小型车队运营商仍可能难以筹集改装车辆所需资本。因此，信贷获取、租赁安排和车队融资可能决定这项技术在大型企业之外得到多广泛的应用。

本地制造和组装改装设备也将变得愈发重要。如果尼日利亚最终能够在本地生产CNG市场所需设备中更大比例的产品，该国便可降低对进口零部件的依赖，同时为汽车产业链内的制造商、技术人员及其他企业创造机会。税收政策的影响并不限于驾车者。不断增长的CNG市场将为车辆经销商、改装中心、零部件供应商、机械师、工程师、运输公司和能源企业带来机会。随着更多车辆转向燃气燃料，对专业维护和技术服务的需求将增长。这可能在尼日利亚汽车行业形成新的专业能力层。传统上专注于汽油和柴油车辆的车间，将越来越需要接受过培训、能够安全检修CNG系统的技术人员。零部件经销商需要了解燃气动力车辆的要求，保险和车辆检验企业也必须适应不断变化的车辆构成。从这个意义上说，CNG转型不仅可以是一项燃料政策，也可以成为一项产业政策。本地能够生产和供应的设备与服务越多，其带来的经济收益就越有可能超越燃油节省本身。

NLCGA提出到2030年将LPG年消费量提高到500万吨的目标，同时支持燃气在交通运输领域得到更广泛采用。政府的税收减免通过降低进口燃气和出行设备的相关成本，提供了重要起点。但其最终成效将取决于这些利益能否转化为更低的购置成本、更多投资和更广的消费者可及性。对投资者而言，问题是尼日利亚能否创建一个足够庞大且稳定的市场，以证明对基础设施和设备投资的合理性。对政府而言，挑战在于确保财政激励措施有配套政策和基础设施支撑，使转型切实可行。

这场始于2023年的行业倡导行动已经演变为一项政策干预，对尼日利亚汽车和运输行业均产生深远影响。取消增值税和进口关税本身并不能保证出行成本下降。燃料价格、汇率、燃气供应、基础设施、车辆成本和维护费用仍会继续影响交通运输的经济格局。但通过取消CNG设备和车辆附带的部分财政成本，政府降低了采用这项技术的一道障碍。如果对加气基础设施的投资与车辆改装同步推进，技术标准保持严格，融资渠道更加便利，供应保持可靠，CNG就可能不再只是政府推动的替代燃料，而有望成为尼日利亚交通体系中具备商业可行性的组成部分。对于一个寻求降低出行成本、同时开发本国天然气资源的国家而言，这一区别至关重要。

因此，衡量增值税和进口关税减免成效的真正标准，并非政府免除了多少税款，而是有多少车辆完成改装、建成了多少加气站、涌现了多少企业，以及最终尼日利亚驾车者能够在多大程度上以更低且更可预测的成本运送人员与货物。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/20/o.summary: An asymmetric warfare veteran and former Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Tukur Yusuf Buratai (rtd), has emphasised the critical role of education in addressing terrorism and insecurity, declaring that “a bullet can kill a terrorist, but only education can kill terrorism”. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/20/o.summary_zh: 一名非对称作战老兵、前陆军参谋长图库尔·优素福·布拉泰中校（已退役）强调，教育在应对恐怖主义和安全问题方面发挥着关键作用，并宣称：“子弹可以杀死恐怖分子，但只有教育才能消灭恐怖主义。”他指出，教育是打击无知、贫困、激进化以及使个人容易受到极端主义意识形态影响的社会环境的有效工具。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/20/o.body: An asymmetric warfare veteran and former Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Tukur Yusuf Buratai (rtd), has emphasised the critical role of education in addressing terrorism and insecurity, declaring that “a bullet can kill a terrorist, but only education can kill terrorism”. He maintained that education is a powerful instrument for combating ignorance, poverty, radicalisation and the social conditions that make individuals vulnerable to extremist ideologies. General Buratai stated this while delivering the 14th convocation lecture to the graduating class of 2026 at Nile University of Nigeria, Abuja. According to him, “A bullet can kill a terrorist. Only education can kill terrorism. I stand before you not merely as a former Chief of Army Staff, but as a soldier who has spent a lifetime confronting a proposition that the world has been slow to accept: that the security of a nation is not measured solely by the strength of its armed forces, but by the strength of its classrooms.” In a lecture titled ‘Nexus Between Education and Security: Implications and Lessons for Sub-Saharan Africa,’ the Chairman of the Tukur Buratai Research Centre (TBRC) said: “Let me begin with a confession. When I was invited to deliver this lecture, I asked myself: ‘What does a soldier have to say to a university?’ “I have spent most of my life in barracks, on training grounds and in theatres of war. You have spent yours in lecture halls, libraries and laboratories. We seem to live in different worlds. “But the longer I thought about it, the more I realised that we live in the same world. We fight the same war. Only our weapons are different. Mine was a rifle. Yours is a pen, a computer, an idea. And I have come to tell you today, from the battlefield of the North-east to the classrooms of the Sahel that your weapon is more powerful than mine.” To further buttress his argument that the pen is mightier than the sword, Buratai recounted a memorable experience from the height of the war against Boko Haram. “Let me begin with a story. A story I have never forgotten. In 2016, during the height of the war against Boko Haram, I visited a liberated community in Borno State. The soldiers had done their job. The terrorists had been pushed out. The market was slowly coming back. “A boy, perhaps 12 years old, walked up to me. He was barefoot. His clothes were torn. He looked up at me and said, ‘Soldier, I want to go to school’. “He pointed to a heap of burnt rubble. That was his school. Boko Haram had burnt it two years earlier. “Then he said something I have never forgotten. He said ‘If I do not go to school, they will come back for me.’ “He was 12 years old. And he understood what many policymakers in Africa still do not understand: that when a school dies, a terrorist is born. That when a child is denied education, an insurgent gains a recruit. “That boy is the reason this lecture is not about guns. It is about books. I do not know where he is today. I pray he is in school. But there are millions like him across sub-Saharan Africa, in Niger, Mali, Burkina Faso, Chad, Somalia, Mozambique, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Sudan. “How we answer that question will determine whether Africa rises or burns in the next thirty years,” he said. Buratai explained that his lecture argues that education and security are not separate domains to be traded off against one another, but two dimensions of a single struggle. “It examines the environment in which this struggle unfolds, the actors who shape it, the reciprocal nexus between learning and violence, the implications for sub-Saharan Africa, and the practical lessons that follow. It draws on published research, official data and the testimony of practitioners, and it concludes with recommendations addressed to policymakers, institutions and the graduating class before whom it is delivered,” the retired Army Chief concluded. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/20/o.title_zh: 布拉塔伊称，只有教育才能击败恐怖主义
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/20/o.body_zh: 一名经历过非对称战争、曾任陆军参谋长的退役中将图库尔·优素福·布拉塔伊强调了教育在应对恐怖主义与不安全局势方面的关键作用，并宣称：“子弹可以杀死恐怖分子，但只有教育才能消灭恐怖主义。”他坚持认为，教育是对抗无知、贫困、激进化以及使个人容易受到极端主义意识形态影响的社会条件的有力工具。布拉塔伊将军是在位于阿布贾的尼日利亚尼罗大学向2026届毕业班发表第14次开学典礼演讲时说出这番话的。据他表示：“子弹可以杀死恐怖分子。只有教育才能消灭恐怖主义。我今天站在你们面前，不只是作为前陆军参谋长，更是作为一名毕生都在应对一种世界迟迟不愿接受的观点的军人：国家安全不能仅以武装力量的实力来衡量，还要以课堂的实力来衡量。”在题为《教育与安全的关联：对撒哈拉以南非洲的影响与经验》的演讲中，图库尔·布拉塔伊研究中心（TBRC）主席说：“让我先作一番坦白。当我受邀发表这场演讲时，我问自己：‘一个军人能对一所大学说些什么？’“我一生中的大部分时间都在军营、训练场和战场上度过。你们的一生则是在阶梯教室、图书馆和实验室里度过的。我们似乎生活在不同的世界里。“但我思考得越久，就越意识到我们生活在同一个世界里。我们进行的是同一场战争，只是我们的武器不同。我的武器是步枪，你们的武器是钢笔、电脑和思想。今天，我要从东北战场来到萨赫勒的课堂，告诉你们：你们的武器比我的更强大。”为进一步论证笔的力量大于剑，布拉塔伊讲述了打击博科哈拉姆战争最激烈时期的一段难忘经历。“让我先讲一个故事，一个我永远无法忘记的故事。2016年，在打击博科哈拉姆战争最激烈的时期，我探访了博尔诺州一个已经解放的社区。士兵们完成了自己的任务，恐怖分子已被赶走，市场正逐渐恢复。 “一个男孩走到我面前，看起来大约12岁。他光着脚，衣服破破烂烂。他抬头看着我说：‘士兵，我想上学。’ “他指向一堆烧焦的瓦砾，那就是他的学校。博科哈拉姆两年前将它烧毁了。 “随后他说了一句我永远无法忘记的话。他说：‘如果我不去上学，他们就会回来找我。’ “他当时12岁，已经懂许多非洲决策者至今仍未明白的道理：学校消亡，恐怖分子就会诞生；孩子被剥夺受教育的机会，叛乱分子就会多一名新兵。 “那个男孩正是这场演讲不以枪炮为主题、而以书籍为主题的原因。我不知道他如今在哪里。我祈祷他正在上学。但撒哈拉以南非洲各地有数百万与他相似的人，包括尼日尔、马里、布基纳法索、乍得、索马里、莫桑比克、刚果民主共和国（DRC）和苏丹。 “我们如何回答这个问题，将决定非洲在未来三十年中是崛起还是燃烧，”他说。布拉塔伊解释说，他的演讲旨在说明，教育与安全并非彼此割裂、只能取舍的两个领域，而是同一场斗争的两个维度。“演讲考察了这场斗争展开的环境、塑造这场斗争的行为者、学习与暴力之间的相互关联、对撒哈拉以南非洲的影响，以及由此得出的实践经验。演讲借鉴了已发表的研究、官方数据和一线实践者的证言，并在结尾向决策者、相关机构和本次演讲的听众——毕业班——提出建议，”这位退役陆军参谋长总结道。THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区以及世界各地设有办公室。作为尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，该报通过全平台服务政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶层，同时为有抱负者和千禧一代提供新思想、文化和技术的交汇点。这份报纸是一项公共信任事业，致力于追求真理与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育和社区，以及人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送电子邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面
